newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Coconut Oil - Prices seen sideways on holidays.
newsitem.headline: Coconut Oil - Prices seen sideways on holidays.

text.p: Coconut oil prices are expected to remain sideways to lower this week as a majority of the market players are still out for the Chinese Lunar New Year and Moslem Eid ul-Fitr festivals, traders said.
"Market will remain quiet. Besides, Kuala Lumpur's crude palm oil futures, physicals and palm kernel oil futures markets are closed from February 6 to 11," said one trader.
"The closure of the Kuala Lumpur market will sideline players since they cannot plot a trend on where the vegetable oil market is heading," another trader said.
Other traders said fresh coconut oil supplies in Rotterdam in the last several days will likely soften prices.
"There were only a handful of buyers last week so I expect stocks to remain at comfortable levels," said one trader.
Traders pegged coconut oil supplies in Rotterdam at 30,913 tonnes as of February 3 against 21,593 tonnes on January 27.
"The increase in stocks could only have come from fresh arrivals," another trader said.

As a result of the rise in coconut oil supplies in Rotterdam, prices of the commodity for February, March and April shipments softened by $5 to $10 per tonne on Saturday, said a trader in one of the largest oleochemicals companies in the Philippines.
"I expect the trend to continue this week with more supplies," the trader added.
Trade group United Coconut Asociation of the Philippines said prices of coconut oil increased to an average of $779 per tonne CIF last week from the previous $770.
Prospects that copra supply from the Philippines would improve in late March or early April is expected to ease prices, another trader said.
